title: Where does a tree come from?

scenes.narration: Hello, I'm Vertie. Today I'm taking apart a tree. A big old oak can weigh as much as ten cars. So where did all that wood come from?
scenes.caption: Where does a tree come from?

scenes.narration: Most people guess the soil. But the soil around an old tree has barely gone down. So the wood is being made somewhere else. In the leaves.
scenes.caption: Not the soil

scenes.narration: Three things reach every leaf. Sunlight from above, water pulled up from the roots, and air, drifting in through tiny pores underneath.
scenes.caption: What goes in

scenes.narration: Something clever happens in there. Let's go inside the leaf and have a look.
scenes.caption: Inside a leaf

scenes.narration: These little green parts are chloroplasts. They catch sunlight, and use its energy to split water apart.
scenes.caption: Catching light

scenes.narration: Then they grab carbon dioxide from the air and build it into sugar. Oxygen is left over, and drifts out for us to breathe.
scenes.caption: Building sugar

scenes.narration: Now, what happens if I take the light away?
scenes.caption: What if...?

scenes.narration: Everything stops. No light, no sugar, and without sugar the plant slowly starves. Right, let's put that back.
Back outside. All that sugar flows from the leaves to every part of the tree, and becomes wood.
scenes.caption: Back outside

scenes.narration: So a tree isn't made of soil at all. It's mostly air and water, stitched together by sunlight.
scenes.caption: Built from thin air
